claims.text: Generative AI models use probabilistic machine learning architectures to infer data distributions and synthesize new data samples.
Large generative AI foundation models exhibit emergence, where capabilities are implicitly induced rather than explicitly constructed.
Large generative AI foundation models exhibit homogenization, enabling a single consolidated model to power diverse downstream systems.
Generative AI models are subject to hallucinations, generating syntactically or semantically plausible content that lacks factual backing.
Training large-scale generative AI models consumes substantial electricity, producing a high carbon footprint.

evidence.description: GPT models can create calendar entries in the .ical format even though such models were not explicitly trained to do so.
Copilot can generate source code across a wide range of programming languages using a single consolidated model.
Training the GPT-3 generative AI model produced an estimated equivalent of 552 metric tons of CO2.

methodologies.name: Socio-Technical Conceptualization Framework for Generative AI
methodologies.description: A three-tier conceptualization mapping generative AI across model-, system-, and application-level perspectives combined with socio-technical dimensions for Information Systems research.

limitations.text: The data modalities depicted in the article's conceptual framework are neither complete nor entirely distinctive.
Generative AI models rely on probabilistic algorithms that produce incorrect or non-verifiable outputs known as hallucinations.
Training generative AI models on biased data amplifies societal stereotypes, toxic language, and demographic biases.
Large neural network architectures in generative AI consume large amounts of electricity during training and operation, causing negative environmental carbon footprint impacts.

future_work.text: Developing algorithmic and user-centered verification mechanisms to detect and mitigate hallucinations in generative AI outputs.
Conducting empirical field experiments to quantify the productivity, economic welfare, and labor market impacts of generative AI.
Establishing socio-technical design principles for developing trustworthy, explainable, and energy-efficient generative AI systems.
